text: CHIEF RE-RANK - ORDER CORRECTED. AuthorizedRemoteRequest (privacy.scala:772) and RemoteCapability (privacy.scala:743) go FIRST, ahead of ValidatedVector. AuthorizedRemoteRequest's own Scaladoc states 'Constructible solely through RemotePolicy.evaluate; the constructor is private so no code path can hand raw text to a remote provider' - fromProduct IS such a code path, so that documented guarantee is currently FALSE. Forging one bypasses RemotePolicy.evaluate's checks on provider allowlist, version-qualified model identity, purpose, expiry, token budget, detector identity and payload digest. RemoteCapability is the same shape carrying expiry, budget, policy id, detector identity and keyed payload digest. This is the privacy boundary deciding whether participant-derived text leaves the machine. DEMONSTRATION FOR THESE TWO IS DIFFERENT: not 'build an invalid value' but 'mint an authorization RemotePolicy.evaluate would have REFUSED' - a capability with a past expiry, or a provider not on the allowlist. WHY THE CHIEF'S ORIGINAL ORDER WAS WRONG, recorded so the heuristic is not reused blindly: the 45 were ranked by whether the COMPANION contained a smart constructor returning Either/Option. AuthorizedRemoteRequest has NO COMPANION OBJECT; its validation lives in RemotePolicy.evaluate, a different object. A search asking 'does this type validate itself' is blind to types validated by an external gate - and externally-gated types are disproportionately the security-relevant ones. Also correcting the bead's own text: of the ten embed-core types, five guard a self-validating constructor, three (SensitiveDigest, EmbedBatch, GeometryPair) validate via differently-named constructors the regex missed, and two validate externally. All ten still close; only the order changes.
